content: To create a new page on WikiDoc, you must be a registered user. If you are not registered, you will need to create an account before proceeding. Once registered, follow these steps to create a new page: Searching for Existing Pages Before creating a new page, it is crucial to determine whether a page on your topic already exists. To search for a specific topic: Enter the desired word or topic into the search box located on the main page and click the Search button. If an exact match exists, you will be directed to that page. Otherwise, you will see a list of pages containing the search term. Review the search results carefully, as the information you are looking for may be categorized under a broader topic. Use the Try Exact Match button for a more precise search. This option will only display pages with the exact title you entered. If you know the exact name of the page you are looking for, this feature allows you to navigate directly to it. For additional tips on effective searching, refer to the WikiDoc search guide. Creating a New Page If no suitable page exists for your topic, you can create a new one. Follow these steps: 1. After searching, if no relevant page is found, you will see a prompt stating, Create the page 'Topic name' on this wiki. Click on the Topic name link to begin creating the page. 2. This will open the edit page for your new topic. 3. This template includes a pre-programmed table of contents for uniformity. To use the template, click Edit on the template page, select all the content, and copy it. Return to your new page's edit screen and paste the copied content. 4. Populate the template with information relevant to your topic, ensuring that each subtopic is addressed appropriately. 5. Once you have completed your edits, click Save Page to publish your work. 6. You can monitor changes to your page by clicking the Watch tab at the top of the page. This feature allows you to track any updates made by other contributors. Creating Special Pages WikiDoc also allows users to create specialized pages for various purposes: User Pages Each registered user has a personal user page to introduce themselves to the WikiDoc community. This page is unique and allows for creative expression. Refer to the user page creation guide for detailed instructions. Board Review Questions The Board Review Questions Project aims to provide a free, accessible repository of original board review questions for medical education. All questions must adhere to WikiDoc's strict anti-plagiarism policies. Questions are reviewed by WikiDoc Scholars and must be approved by the Editors-in-Chief before being uploaded. For more information, consult the board review question creation guide. Crowdiagnosis Pages The Crowdiagnosis Project, also known as Operation Zebra, focuses on compiling comprehensive lists of potential causes for symptoms, signs, and laboratory abnormalities. These lists are initially generated using artificial intelligence and then refined by medical professionals worldwide. For guidance on creating a Crowdiagnosis page, refer to the relevant instructions. Critical Pathways Pages Critical pathways are evidence-based management tools designed for specific patient groups with predictable clinical courses. These pathways optimize care by defining and sequencing interventions. WikiDoc supports the creation of such pages to improve patient outcomes and reduce healthcare costs. Refer to the critical pathways page creation guide for details. Guidelines Pages The Guidelines Project provides summaries of the latest medical research and treatment recommendations. It is intended for healthcare professionals at all levels to contribute their expertise. This project emphasizes evidence-based practices to enhance medical education and patient care. For instructions, consult the guidelines page creation guide. Microchaptered Pages A microchapter is a smaller subsection of a larger chapter. For example, a disease like pericarditis may have microchapters such as Pericarditis Overview, Pericarditis Pathophysiology, and Pericarditis Treatment. For more information, refer to the microchaptered page creation guide. Resident Survival Guide Pages The Resident Survival Guide Project is a collaborative effort to provide practical resources for medical trainees. These guides address common medical conditions encountered during training and emphasize evidence-based approaches to diagnosis and treatment. For guidance, consult the resident survival guide page creation instructions. Patient Information Pages Patient information pages are designed to provide clear, patient-oriented explanations of medical conditions, including background, diagnosis, and treatment options. For instructions, refer to the patient information page creation guide. Editing Pages If you wish to edit an existing page, you can contribute by improving its content. Use the editor's tools for guidance on creating references, adding links, and making other edits. If you find a preexisting page related to your topic, feel free to enhance its content constructively. For detailed instructions, refer to the page editing guide.
